title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 49 (Calls on Shares of Same Class to Be Made on Uniform Basis)

content.overview: Where calls for further share capital are made on shares of a class, the calls must be made on a uniform basis on all shares of that class.
content.glance: Where calls for further share capital are made on shares of a class, the calls must be made on a uniform basis on all shares of that class.
content.study: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 49 (Calls on shares of same class to be made on uniform basis). Where calls for further share capital are made on shares of a class, the calls must be made on a uniform basis on all shares of that class. Identify the class and compare the terms of the call applied to each share in that class. Do not confuse a call made by the company with a member's voluntary payment in advance under section 50 or the dividend calculation rule in section 51.

sections.heading: Trigger
sections.body: The company makes a call for further share capital on shares belonging to a class.

sections.heading: Uniformity requirement
sections.body: The call must be made on a uniform basis across all shares falling within that class.

sections.heading: Distinction from related provisions
sections.body: Section 49 concerns company calls. Section 50 concerns voluntary acceptance of uncalled capital before it is called; section 51 concerns proportional dividend where the articles authorise it.

provisions.title: Calls on shares of same class to be made on uniform basis

examples.title: Uniform call
examples.body: The company calls ₹10 per share on all partly paid equity shares of the same class. Section 49 is complied with.

examples.title: Discriminatory call
examples.body: The board calls further capital only on some shareholders within the same class. Section 49 is breached.

hypotheticals.question: Can the company call different amounts on different shares of the same class?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 49 requires calls on a uniform basis on all shares falling under that class.

distinctions.title: Calls and advance payment
distinctions.left: Section 49 requires uniform company calls on shares of a class.
distinctions.right: Section 50 permits advance payment of uncalled capital if the articles authorise it.

rows.right: Articles authority and no voting rights until payable

misconceptions.trap: The company may call only selected holders within a class for convenience.
misconceptions.correction: Section 49 mandates uniform calls on all shares of that class.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What does uniformity mean under section 49?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Calls for further share capital must be made on a uniform basis for all shares in the same class.

questionsAndAnswers.question: Is section 49 the rule for voluntary advance payment before a call?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: No. That subject is addressed by section 50, including its articles-authorisation and voting provisions.
